recipes.name: 3 Course Dinner inspired by Drop
ingredients: 1 tbsp brown sugar or coconut sugar
2 tbsp fruity, extra virgin olive oil
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
8 oz Kobe filet or well marbled filet
4 oz goat cheese, at room temperature
instructions: For Duck Breast Salad:
For the Duck

Pat the duck breasts completely dry, then score the fatty side with a very tight pattern, about ¼” wide. Use almost no pressure when scoring, making sure to only score the skin, and avoid cutting down into the flesh of the duck. - 2 (8 oz) duck breasts
After scoring both duck breasts, season the fatty side with kosher salt. - kosher salt - 2 (8 oz) duck breasts
Place skinside up on a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet and refrigerate for at least 1 day and up to 4 days. - For the Duck
While the duck is dry brining, make the pickled red onions.
For the Pickled Red Onions
Slice the onion into rounds and separate the slices. - 1 large red onion
Then, transfer to a sealable container and add mustard seeds. Set aside. - 2 tsp mustard seed - 1 large red onion

In a small saucepot over medium heat, combine red wine vinegar, water, sugar, and kosher salt. Mix until dissolved. Then, rapidly cool with the ice cubes. - 1 cup red wine vinegar - ½ cup water - 2 tbsp sugar - 1 tsp kosher salt - ½ cup ice cubes
Transfer the cooled pickling liquid to the sealable container with the sliced red onions making sure the onions are completely submerged. - For the Pickling Liquid - For the Pickled Red Onion
Refrigerate at least overnight or up to 1 week. - For the Pickled Red Onion
For the Sauces
For the Mango Sauce

In a medium saucepan over medium heat, combine chicken stock, chopped shallot, Fresno chiles, garlic clove, ground ginger, lemongrass, mango nectar, white wine vinegar, and brown sugar or coconut sugar. - 1 cup chicken stock - ½ small shallot chopped - ½ small Fresno chili thinly sliced - 1 garlic clove smashed - 1 tsp ground ginger - ½ stick lemongrass microplaned - 1 cup mango nectar - 1 tbsp white wine vinegar - 1 tbsp brown sugar or coconut sugar
Bring to a simmer, then cook for about 10 minutes, or until the aromatics soften. Season to taste with kosher salt. - kosher salt
Transfer mixture to a blender and blitz on high speed until completely smooth.
While the blender is running, add xanthan gum ¼ tsp at a time until the sauce coats the back of a spoon, about ¾ tsp. - ¾ tsp xanthan gum
Taste again for seasoning then transfer to a glass bowl, cover, and chill until ready to use. - For the Mango Ginger Sauce
For the Pomegranate Sauce

In a medium saucepan over medium heat, combine pomegranate juice, chicken stock, honey, white pepper, ground coriander, and white wine vinegar. - 1 cup pomegranate juice - 1 cup chicken stock - ¼ cup honey - ¼ tsp white pepper - ¼ tsp ground coriander - splash white wine vinegar
Bring to a simmer, then cook for about 10 minutes, or until the aromatics soften.
Transfer mixture to a blender and blitz on high speed until completely smooth.
While the blender is running, add xanthan gum ¼ tsp at a time until the sauce coats the back of a spoon, about ¾ tsp. - ¾ tsp xanthan gum
Taste again for seasoning then transfer to a glass bowl, cover, and chill until ready to use. - For the Pomegranate Sauce
For the Dressing

In a small bowl, combine the lime juice, candied ginger, olive oil, garlic clove, kosher salt, freshly ground black pepper, and honey. - 1 lime juiced - candied ginger - 2 tbsp fruity extra virgin olive oil - 1 clove garlic microplaned - kosher salt - freshly ground black pepper - 1 tbsp honey
Tiny whisk or cover and shake into a thick, creamy dressing. Prepare the day before serving and refrigerate.
For the Salad

Combine all the greens, tri-colored carrot curls, pickled red onions, and candied ginger in a large salad bowl. Set aside while you fry your duck. - butter leaf lettuce - red lettuce - dandelion greens - tri colored carrot curls - Pickled Red Onions - candied ginger
For the Duck
Place the dry-brined duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, ungreased stainless steel pan. Weigh the breasts down if possible to ensure even contact. - For the Duck
Turn the heat on low and rotate the pan frequently, gently rendering out the fat for 5 minutes. - For the Duck

The duck should not make a sound during this time. If you hear any crackling, popping, or hissing, immediately remove from heat until silent. Then return to the heat and continue to render the fat. - For the Duck
After 5 minutes, the duck should be swimming in its own fat. - For the Duck

Then, increase the heat slightly to maintain a gentle bubble in the fat without any cooking sounds from the duck breast for 10 minutes until the duck skin becomes golden brown and crisp. - For the Duck
Season with flaky finishing salt, flip, and cook for 5 more minutes or until the thickest point of the duck registers at 125°F. - flaky finishing salt - For the Duck
Transfer the duck breasts to a wire cooling rack set inside a rimmed baking sheet to drain and cool for 5 to 10 minutes, reserving the duck fat in the pan. - For the Duck
For the Assembly

Toast the cashews over medium low heat in the same pan with the reserved duck fat for 2-3 minutes until brown and crisp. Using a kitchen spider, transfer to a plate of paper towels to drain. - toasted cashews
Pour the salad dressing over the top of the greens in the salad bowl and toss vigorously. - For the Dressing - For the Salad
Pile the greens on one side of a large, white serving plate and top with the toasted cashews. - For the Salad - toasted cashews
Dot the other side of the plate with 3 small dots of the Pomegranate sauce aside 2 large dots of Mango Ginger sauce. - For the Pomegranate Sauce - For the Mango Ginger Sauce
Slice the duck into bite-sized pieces and plate in a row along the center of the plate. - For the Duck
Finally, top with candied ginger and serve immediately! - candied ginger
For Filet Mignon with Truffle Mashed Potatoes:
For the Truffle Mashed Potatoes
Peel and chop the potatoes into uniform pieces then transfer to separate pots of cold, lightly salted water. - 3 russet potatoes - 3 Yukon gold potatoes - kosher salt to taste
Add the crushed garlic. - 2 cloves garlic crushed
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium high heat and cook the Russet Potatoes for anywhere from 12-18 minutes until they are very tender but not falling apart. - 3 russet potatoes
Cook the Yukon Potatoes will need to steam for about 10 minutes longer. - 3 Yukon gold potatoes
Combine and pass the cooked potatoes through a fine mesh sieve or a ricer. - For the Truffle Mashed Potatoes

Then, return the potatoes to the same pot over low heat and add heavy cream and black truffle butter. Mix to combine and season with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper. - 1 cup warm heavy cream - 2 oz tub black truffle butter - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste
Mix and cook over low heat for about 30 seconds. - For the Truffle Mashed Potatoes
Then transfer to your oven-safe serving vessel or cast iron pan, allowing it to cool completely before covering and refrigerating until ready to serve. - For the Truffle Mashed Potatoes

To serve, remove from the fridge and allow the potatoes to return to room temperature before topping with crushed black truffle potato chips and drizzle with the reserved duck fat. - truffle potato chip topping - For the Truffle Mashed Potatoes
Bake uncovered at 375°F for 20 to 30 minutes or until bubbling and lightly brown. - For the Truffle Mashed Potatoes
Garnish with freshly picked thyme leaves, serve hot, and enjoy! - fresh thyme leaves - For the Truffle Mashed Potatoes
For the Filet Mignon
For the Filet
Trim off the extra fat and connective tissue. - 8 oz Kobe filet or well marbled filet
Then, salt all sides and dry brine in the fridge for at least 2 hours and up to overnight. - kosher salt to taste - 8 oz Kobe filet or well marbled filet
For the Red Miso Butter
In a mixing bowl, combine red miso paste, soy sauce, and softened butter. - 2 tbsp red miso paste - 1 tsp soy sauce - 4 oz softened unsalted butter
Whisk until homogeneous. Set aside.
For the Demi-Glace
In a medium saucepan, combine demi, unpeeled garlic cloves, shallot, and pinot noir. - 16 oz store bought demi sauce - 6 cloves garlic unpeeled & halved - 1 small shallot halved - 1 tbsp pinot noir
Reduce over medium heat to about ¼ of the mixture’s original volume. - For the Demi Glace
Pass through a fine mesh sieve and refrigerate until ready to serve. - For the Demi Glace
To serve, return to a saucepan, bring to a bare simmer, kill the heat. - For the Demi Glace
When the bubbles have stopped, whisk in Red Miso Butter until it becomes a thick sauce. - 2 tbsp Red Miso Butter - For the Demi Glace
For the Vegetables
Preheat the oven to 375°F with convection.
Prep a whole head of the mushroom in a small, oven-safe pan. - 1 large oyster or Maitake mushroom
Generously drizzle with extra virgin olive oil making sure to rub it down into the mushroom. - extra virgin olive oil
Then, generously brush with Red Miso butter. Season with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper. - Red Miso butter - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground pepper
Transfer to the oven and roast for 25 to 35 minutes or until deeply golden brown and crisp. - 1 large oyster or Maitake mushroom
Meanwhile, sauté carrots in a saucepan with vegetable oil and a splash of water. - 4 medium multicolored carrots - vegetable oil
Cover and allow the steam to cook the carrots over low heat until tender. - 4 medium multicolored carrots
Once the carrots are tender, add a splash of soy sauce, fresh thyme leaves and freshly ground pepper. - 1 tsp soy sauce - fresh thyme leaves - freshly ground pepper - 4 medium multicolored carrots
Then, transfer to the oven at 375°F and roast for 5-10 minutes, uncovered. Toss occasionally until browned all over. - 4 medium multicolored carrots
For the Filet
Season with salt and pepper, oil, and bring a carbon steel pan to high heat (ripping hot). - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground pepper - vegetable oil
Place filet in the well-seasoned, ripping hot pan. - 8 oz Kobe filet or well marbled filet
Develop a rich, brown crust on all sides then transfer to the 375°F oven. - 8 oz Kobe filet or well marbled filet
Flip the filet every 5 minutes until it reaches an internal temp of 125°F at its thickest point. - 8 oz Kobe filet or well marbled filet
Remove from the oven and let it rest for 5 minutes before carving. - 8 oz Kobe filet or well marbled filet
For the Serving
Pour the fortified demi-glace into a Sake cup. - For the Demi Glace
Stack the roasted carrots in an avant garde fashion along with the roasted mushroom on a serving plate. - 4 medium multicolored carrots
Then, slice the steak in half and plate. - 8 oz Kobe filet or well marbled filet
Serve hot, optionally with truffle mashed potatoes. - For the Truffle Mashed Potatoes
For Panna Cotta:
For the Panna Cotta
To a medium saucepan, add cream, sugar and salt. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally. - 2 cups heavy cream - ⅔ cup sugar (132g) - ¼ tsp kosher salt
Place buttermilk in a cup. Sprinkle gelatin over top. Allow to bloom for 5-10 minutes while cream comes to a simmer. - 1 cup buttermilk - 1 packet powdered gelatin

When cream comes to a simmer, lower the heat and whisk in buttermilk/gelatin mixture. Whisk until gelatin is dissolved. Place softened goat cheese in a bowl. Whisk cream mixture into goat cheese, one ladleful at a time, until completely combined. - 4 oz goat cheese at room temperature
Strain panna cotta base through a sieve into a large liquid measuring cup. Pour mixture into silicone molds. Cool at room temperature. - For the Panna Cotta
Place in the fridge to cool and set up completely for several hours or ideally overnight. - For the Panna Cotta
For the Pomegranate Pearls
Pour oil into a tall glass and chill (the oil must be cold). - vegetable oil

In a very small saucepan, add the juice, rosemary, vanilla, salt and sugar, and bring to a boil. Add agar agar, reduce to a gentle simmer and cook 1-2 minutes, or until agar agar is dissolved. - ⅓ cup pomegranate juice - 1 sprig fresh rosemary - ¼ tsp vanilla extract - of kosher salt - 2 tbsp coconut sugar - ¼ tsp agar agar
Let cool for 3-5 minutes. Strain out solids. - For the Pomegranate Pearls

Fill a syringe or squeeze bottle with the juice. Drop one drop at a time into the cold oil. Little caviar orbs will form on contact with the cold oil and fall to the bottom. Do this while the liquid is still somewhat warm, or it will solidify in the bottle! - For the Pomegranate Pearls - vegetable oil
Strain caviar using a fine mesh strainer. Rinse well with water. - For the Pomegranate Pearls
Store caviar in water until ready to use. - For the Pomegranate Pearls
Lay on a paper towel-lined plate and pat dry.
For the Serving
Carefully invert the set panna cotta onto a serving plate. Then, top with the Pomegranate Cavier. Serve immediately and enjoy! - Panna Cotta - Pomegranate Pearls (Cavier)
